summary: Phase 1 regression for spec fixes #1, #8, #9, #10, #11, #12, #13, #18. Backend: 2 pass, 2 skip (no linked accounts on test user; tz_aware=True verified directly against Motor → datetimes come back UTC-aware, isoformat includes '+00:00'). Frontend: #1, #10, #11, #13 PASS. #18 FAIL — auto-scroll does NOT bring the current-month pill (Aug) into view on mount; pill is fixed at x=473 (offscreen for 390px viewport) after 4s of settle time. RCA: useEffect that calls scrollRef.scrollTo runs BEFORE onLayout populates pillOffsets ref, so it early-returns and never re-runs. #8 partial: test user has no linked accounts so no 'Last synced …' string was rendered on Wealth (banner shows 'No accounts linked yet'); backend tz-aware Mongo probe confirms the ISO output ends in '+00:00'. No hard console errors ('is not defined' / 'Cannot read propert'); only pre-existing shadow* deprecation + iframe sandbox warnings.

minor.issue: Test user alex+test1 has 0 linked accounts, so runtime confirmation of last_sync_at containing '+00:00' from a real Plaid/SimpleFIN row was not possible. Verified indirectly: (1) code path at server.py:776/1495 calls `last_sync.isoformat()` on Mongo-returned datetime; (2) direct Motor probe with AsyncIOMotorClient(MONGO_URL, tz_aware=True) round-trips a UTC datetime and returns tzinfo=FixedOffset(0) → isoformat='2026-08-11T22:43:56.879000+00:00'. ui_bugs.issue: Budget period strip does NOT auto-scroll the current-month pill into view on mount. Pill 'budget-period-Aug' bounding_box.x = 473 (viewport width 390), so 'Aug' is fully offscreen to the right. Polled at 500ms/1s/2s/4s after Budget nav — position never changes. Same issue affects tx-month strip and any long scrollable PeriodPills group. Reference: /app/frontend/src/utils/appShared.tsx:158-166.

action_items: FIX #18 auto-scroll: PeriodPills useEffect at appShared.tsx:158-166 fires on mount BEFORE the pill's onLayout populates pillOffsets/pillWidths refs, so the guard `typeof offset === 'number'` short-circuits and scrollTo never runs. Suggested fix: trigger the scroll from inside the pill's onLayout callback when v === value (i.e., detect that this is the layout event for the currently-selected pill and call scrollRef.current.scrollTo immediately with the freshly-measured x/width). Alternatively promote pillOffsets to state so the useEffect re-runs after onLayout, or call requestAnimationFrame in the effect. The current implementation only works when `value` CHANGES (post-mount navigation), not on initial mount which is the primary user-facing case.

Retest #8 end-to-end after a Plaid/SimpleFIN account is linked to the test user. Backend code path was verified via a direct Motor round-trip (isoformat includes '+00:00'); no real bank last_sync_at could be observed because alex+test1 has 0 linked accounts.
critical_code_review_comments: appShared.tsx PeriodPills auto-scroll effect assumes onLayout has already fired by the time useEffect runs — this is a well-known React Native race. The effect should either (a) trigger from onLayout when the selected pill is measured, or (b) store offsets in state so the effect re-runs. As written, spec #18 only satisfies the 'on change' half of the requirement, not the 'on mount' half.

rca_of_issue: #18 auto-scroll bug — /app/frontend/src/utils/appShared.tsx:158-166. On first mount, React renders → useEffect([value, scrollable]) fires with pillOffsets.current empty → early return. onLayout callbacks on each Pressable then populate pillOffsets/pillWidths refs, but React does NOT re-run the effect because refs mutating does not trigger renders. Net result: the scroll only fires on subsequent value changes, never on mount. Reproduction: log in → tap nav-budget → observe `budget-period-Aug` at x=473 in a 390px viewport (offscreen right, requires manual scroll). Mitigation: capture the layout event for the selected pill inside onLayout and call scrollRef.current.scrollTo directly when v === value, OR promote offsets/widths to state (memoized) so the effect re-runs, OR wrap scrollTo in requestAnimationFrame or setTimeout(0) inside the effect (last resort — still racey).
